niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your objectives (brand awareness vs. direct response), budget, geography, target audience, required inventory (streamers vs. programmatic), and measurement needs. Below is a short framework to help you pick plus a practical shortlist of well-regarded options by use case.

Quick clarifying questions (so I can recommend a specific agency):
- Are you a brand advertiser, direct-response / performance marketer, or an agency buying for clients?
- Primary goal: reach/awareness, lower-funnel conversions, or a mix?
- Budget range and target geography (US, EMEA, global)?
- Do you need creative production as well as media buying?

Who to consider (by type and use case)
- Large global/full-service media agencies (best for big brands, cross-channel planning, premium inventory access)
  - GroupM (Wavemaker, Mindshare) — deep publisher relationships and TV/CTV scale
  - Omnicom Media Group (OMD, PHD) — integrated planning and data
  - Publicis Media (Starcom, Zenith) — planning + programmatic expertise
  - Dentsu (Carat) and IPG Mediabrands (Initiative, UM)

- CTV-native / performance-focused specialists (best for direct-response, ROI-driven campaigns)
  - MNTN — performance CTV platform + creative for direct-response
  - Tinuiti — strong performance/retail media and CTV execution for e-commerce brands

- Programmatic/technology-first partners (DSPs and platform partners — used by agencies and brands)
  - The Trade Desk — widely used DSP for programmatic CTV buying
  - Roku OneView — publisher/platform for Roku-native buys and measurement
  - Tremor Video / Xandr-style DSPs — programmatic CTV access and targeting

- Creative, interactive, and measurement specialists (use alongside media buyers)
  - Innovid — personalized/interactive CTV creative and measurement
  - BrightLine — interactive CTV creative and experiences
  - VideoAmp, Samba TV — cross-screen measurement, attribution, and audience data

How to choose the best partner
- Align on goals: brand lift vs. conversions changes agency choice and pricing model.
- Inventory & publisher access: ask which platforms/publishers they can guarantee (Roku, Hulu, Peacock, network VOD, programmatic exchanges).
- Measurement & attribution: request third-party measurement (Samba TV, Nielsen, VideoAmp) and clear KPIs.
- Creative capability: do they produce CTV-friendly creative (long-form, interactive, dynamic)?
- Data & targeting: household graph, addressable, audience segments, frequency capping.
- Transparency & fees: media transparency, reporting cadence, and the agency’s fee model.
- Proven results: request relevant case studies, references, and campaign metrics.

Next steps I can help with
- Shortlist 3–5 agencies based on your answers to the questions above
- Draft an RFP template and list of questions to evaluate CTV partners
- Compare proposals if you already have responses

Tell me your goals, budget range, and geography and I’ll recommend a short, tailored list.
